title: My reflection was a second late 🪞
style_prompt: dark blue cinematic night, faceless silhouette, fog, minimal interior, no text, no watermark
hook_text: At 2:31 in the morning my reflection in the bathroom mirror blinked one second after I did.

scenes.narration: At 2:31 in the morning my reflection in the bathroom mirror blinked one second after I did.
I thought I was tired. I raised my hand to rub my eyes. My reflection waited, then raised its hand, slow and careful, copying me.
I stepped back. The reflection stayed exactly where it was for a full second, then stepped back too, as if it were learning the move.
I tried to laugh it off. I counted the delay. One second. Then a second and a half. Every time I moved, it needed longer to catch up.
So I stood completely still. My reflection did not. It tilted its head, and looked down at the sink, and slowly picked up my toothbrush.
I had not moved. I could see my own hands at my sides, and in the glass the toothbrush rose in a hand that was not mine.
It brushed. Calmly, evenly, like somebody settling into a new home. Then it turned the tap and I heard water that was not running in the room.
It leaned forward until its face filled the glass and whispered, you can go to bed now, I will be you in the morning. And my own mouth opened, and said, goodnight.
So tell me. Do you smash the mirror, or turn the light off?
